Domain-1.overview:
AI Data Sovereignty addresses your organization's control over data used for AI/ML training, inference, and operations. This includes training datasets, real-time inference data, model outputs, and data pipelines.
  • Data Residency Control: Ensures AI training and inference data remains within authorized jurisdictions.
  • Data Quality & Lineage: Maintains control over data provenance, labeling, and quality for AI workloads.
  • Privacy Protection: Ensures sensitive data used in AI models complies with privacy regulations.
  • Data Pipeline Independence: Maintains autonomous control over data collection, processing, and storage for AI.
Domain-1.title: AI Data Sovereignty
Domain-1.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Where is your AI training data stored and processed?
  • Do you have policies restricting AI data to specific jurisdictions?
  • Can you prove training data never leaves approved regions?
  • How do you handle cross-border data for model training?
Domain-1.1-recommendation:
What is AI Training Data Residency?

AI Training Data Residency ensures that all data used to train machine learning models remains within designated geographic and jurisdictional boundaries. Unlike traditional data residency, AI training often involves massive datasets that may be processed across distributed infrastructure, creating unique sovereignty challenges.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a formal AI Data Residency Policy that mandates geographic restrictions on where training datasets can be stored, processed, and accessed. This policy must cover both structured data warehouses and unstructured data lakes used for AI/ML workloads.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy AI training infrastructure on sovereign cloud regions or on-premises data centers where physical location is certified and auditable. Implement data governance tools that track data lineage throughout the AI pipeline and prevent accidental data movement across jurisdictional boundaries.
Domain-1.1-redhat-description: Software-defined storage solution providing data services for AI/ML workloads with geo-replication control, ensuring training data remains within sovereign boundaries while maintaining high performance for GPU workloads.
Domain-1.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Where does inference data (user inputs/outputs) get stored?
  • Do you encrypt inference data at rest and in transit?
  • How do you handle PII in model inputs/outputs?
  • Are inference logs subject to privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA)?
Domain-1.2-recommendation:
What is AI Inference Data Protection?

AI Inference Data Protection ensures that data submitted to AI models for predictions (inputs) and the resulting outputs are protected throughout their lifecycle. Inference data often contains sensitive user information and must be protected from unauthorized access or cross-border transfer.

Executive Recommendations

Implement Privacy-by-Design principles for all AI inference endpoints, ensuring user data is encrypted, access-controlled, and retained only as long as necessary. Establish clear data retention policies for inference logs and model outputs.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy inference services with end-to-end encryption, ensuring data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest. Implement data tokenization or anonymization for sensitive inference data where possible, and ensure inference logs are stored in sovereign-controlled infrastructure.
Domain-1.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Who labels your training data (internal teams vs. third-party vendors)?
  • Where are data labeling operations performed?
  • Do you have control over labeling quality and bias?
  • Can labeling vendors access your raw data?
Domain-1.3-recommendation:
What is AI Data Labeling Control?

AI Data Labeling Control ensures that the process of annotating and labeling training data remains under organizational control, preventing third-party vendors from accessing sensitive raw data or introducing bias through labeling processes.

Executive Recommendations

Establish internal data labeling capabilities or use sovereign-approved labeling services that operate under strict contractual and jurisdictional controls. Require labeling vendors to sign data processing agreements that prohibit data transfer outside approved jurisdictions.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy self-hosted labeling platforms or use privacy-preserving techniques where labeling can be performed on encrypted or anonymized data. Implement quality control processes to detect and mitigate bias in labeled datasets.
Domain-1.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you use synthetic data to augment training datasets?
  • Where are synthetic data generation models hosted?
  • Can you generate synthetic data independently without vendor tools?
  • How do you ensure synthetic data quality and representativeness?
Domain-1.4-recommendation:
What is Synthetic Data Generation Sovereignty?

Synthetic Data Generation Sovereignty enables organizations to create artificial training data that mirrors real-world patterns without exposing sensitive information, reducing reliance on external data sources and third-party synthetic data vendors.

Executive Recommendations

Invest in internal synthetic data generation capabilities, particularly for regulated industries where real data sharing is restricted. Establish quality metrics to ensure synthetic data accurately represents real-world distributions.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy open-source synthetic data generation frameworks on sovereign infrastructure. Use generative models (GANs, VAEs) to create realistic synthetic datasets that can be shared more freely than real data while maintaining privacy.
Domain-1.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you trace data lineage from source to trained model?
  • Do you have audit logs of all data transformations?
  • Can you reproduce training datasets used for specific model versions?
  • How do you detect unauthorized data access in AI pipelines?
Domain-1.5-recommendation:
What is Data Pipeline Auditability?

Data Pipeline Auditability provides complete visibility into how data flows through AI/ML workflows, from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, feature engineering, and model training, enabling forensic analysis and compliance verification.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate comprehensive audit logging for all AI data pipelines, ensuring data lineage can be traced for compliance and incident investigation. Implement data versioning to enable reproducibility of training experiments.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy MLOps platforms with built-in data lineage tracking. Use immutable storage for training datasets and implement cryptographic hashing to verify data integrity. Ensure all data access events are logged to a sovereign-controlled SIEM.
Domain-1.5-redhat-description: Enterprise MLOps platform with built-in data lineage tracking, experiment versioning, and audit logging capabilities, enabling complete traceability of data flows throughout the AI lifecycle.
Domain-1.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you know the source and origin of all training data?
  • Can you verify data quality and bias metrics before training?
  • How do you handle third-party datasets (licenses, terms)?
  • Do you have processes to detect data poisoning attempts?
Domain-1.6-recommendation:
What is Training Data Provenance?

Training Data Provenance establishes a verifiable chain of custody for all data used in model training, ensuring data sources are known, licensed appropriately, and free from malicious manipulation or poisoning.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a Data Registry that catalogs all training datasets with metadata including source, license, quality metrics, and approval status. Require legal review of third-party datasets before use in production models.

Technical Recommendations

Implement automated data quality checks and bias detection before datasets are approved for training. Use cryptographic signatures to verify dataset integrity and detect tampering or data poisoning attempts.
Domain-1.7: Real-time Data Flow Monitoring for AI
Domain-1.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you monitor data flows in real-time across AI pipelines?
  • Do you have alerts for unauthorized data transfers?
  • Can you detect data exfiltration attempts from AI systems?
  • How do you ensure inference data doesn't leak to unauthorized systems?
Domain-1.7-recommendation:
What is Real-time Data Flow Monitoring?

Real-time Data Flow Monitoring tracks all data movements within AI infrastructure, detecting and blocking unauthorized transfers, data exfiltration, or policy violations before they occur.

Executive Recommendations

Deploy continuous monitoring solutions that provide real-time visibility into AI data flows with automated alerting for policy violations. Require quarterly audits of data flow logs to identify anomalies.

Technical Recommendations

Implement network traffic analysis and DLP tools specifically configured for AI/ML workloads. Use service mesh technologies to monitor and control data flows between AI microservices and external systems.
Domain-1.7-redhat-description: Provides complete network traffic control and observability for AI microservices with fine-grained policies to monitor and restrict data flows, preventing unauthorized data transfers in real-time.
Domain-1.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Which third parties (cloud providers, vendors) can access your AI training data?
  • Do you use Just-in-Time access for vendor support of AI systems?
  • Can you revoke vendor access to AI data immediately?
  • Where are AI vendor support personnel located geographically?
Domain-1.8-recommendation:
What is Third-Party AI Data Access Control?

Third-Party AI Data Access Control regulates when and how external vendors, cloud providers, or contractors can access AI training data, models, and inference systems, preventing unauthorized access that could compromise sovereignty.

Executive Recommendations

Develop and enforce a Third-Party AI Data Access Policy that defines clear time-limited thresholds for vendor access to AI systems and data. Require annual re-vetting of all vendors with privileged access.

Technical Recommendations

Enforce Just-in-Time (JIT) access and ephemeral credentials for all third-party access to AI infrastructure. Channel all vendor access through monitored jump boxes with session recording. Implement automated revocation when vendor contracts expire.

Domain-2.overview:
AI Model Sovereignty ensures your organization maintains ownership, transparency, and control over the AI models deployed in production. This includes model architecture, weights, training processes, and the ability to inspect, modify, and port models independently.
  • Model Ownership: Full rights to model architecture, parameters, and artifacts.
  • Transparency & Explainability: Ability to understand and explain model decisions and behavior.
  • Portability: Freedom to deploy models across different infrastructure without vendor lock-in.
  • Intellectual Property Control: Protection of proprietary model innovations and techniques.
Domain-2.title: AI Model Sovereignty
Domain-2.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you own the architecture of your AI models or use vendor-proprietary models?
  • Can you access and modify model architectures?
  • Are you using open-source model architectures or closed black-box models?
  • Can you rebuild models from scratch if vendor relationships end?
Domain-2.1-recommendation:
What is Model Architecture Ownership?

Model Architecture Ownership ensures you have full rights and access to the structural design of your AI models, enabling independent modification, optimization, and deployment without vendor dependencies.

Executive Recommendations

Prioritize open-source model architectures (transformers, CNNs, RNNs) over proprietary vendor models. Ensure all custom model development includes full IP ownership clauses in contracts with development partners.

Technical Recommendations

Use open-source ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX) for model development. Document all model architectures in version control and ensure architecture definitions are stored in human-readable formats (YAML, JSON).
Domain-2.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you access and export trained model weights?
  • Where are model checkpoints stored?
  • Do you have version control for model parameters?
  • Can you fine-tune models or are they frozen by the vendor?
Domain-2.2-recommendation:
What is Model Weights Access?

Model Weights Access ensures you can access, export, and control the trained parameters of your AI models, enabling fine-tuning, optimization, and migration to different infrastructure.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate that all trained models must be exportable in standard formats (ONNX, SavedModel, checkpoint files). Prohibit use of AI services that restrict access to model weights or parameters.

Technical Recommendations

Store model weights in sovereign-controlled artifact repositories with versioning. Use standard serialization formats that enable cross-framework compatibility. Implement automated backup of model checkpoints to prevent data loss.
Domain-2.2-redhat-description: Sovereign-controlled enterprise container registry that can store ML model artifacts, versioned model containers, and model checkpoints with geo-replication control and security scanning.
Domain-2.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you explain how your AI models make decisions?
  • Do you use explainability tools (SHAP, LIME, etc.)?
  • Are model decision processes auditable for compliance?
  • Can you demonstrate model fairness and bias metrics?
Domain-2.3-recommendation:
What is Model Interpretability?

Model Interpretability ensures you can understand, explain, and audit AI model decisions, critical for regulatory compliance (EU AI Act), ethical AI, and building stakeholder trust.

Executive Recommendations

Establish Model Explainability Standards requiring all production models to provide decision explanations for regulated use cases. Invest in explainability tools and training for data science teams.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate explainability frameworks (SHAP, LIME, integrated gradients) into the model deployment pipeline. Generate and store explanation artifacts alongside model predictions for audit purposes.
Domain-2.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you track all versions of deployed AI models?
  • Can you trace which data was used to train specific model versions?
  • Can you rollback to previous model versions if needed?
  • Do you maintain metadata for all model experiments?
Domain-2.4-recommendation:
What is Model Versioning & Lineage?

Model Versioning & Lineage provides complete traceability of model evolution, training data, hyperparameters, and deployment history, enabling reproducibility and compliance verification.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate use of MLOps platforms that automatically track model lineage, versioning, and metadata. Require model versioning for all production deployments with ability to rollback within SLA timeframes.

Technical Recommendations

Use MLOps tools with built-in experiment tracking and model registry capabilities. Implement semantic versioning for models and store all training artifacts (code, data versions, hyperparameters) alongside model versions.
Domain-2.4-redhat-description: Enterprise MLOps platform providing comprehensive model versioning, lineage tracking, and experiment management with full auditability and reproducibility for sovereign AI operations.
Domain-2.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you understand the licenses of all models you use (including pre-trained models)?
  • Can you use models for commercial purposes without restrictions?
  • Do you have IP ownership of custom-developed models?
  • Are there export restrictions on models you deploy?
Domain-2.5-recommendation:
What is Model Licensing Control?

Model Licensing Control ensures clarity on intellectual property rights, usage restrictions, and commercial permissions for all AI models, preventing legal and compliance issues.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a Model License Registry cataloging all models with license terms, usage restrictions, and commercial permissions. Require legal review of pre-trained model licenses before production deployment.

Technical Recommendations

Implement automated license scanning in the model deployment pipeline. Maintain clear separation between models with different licensing terms (e.g., GPL vs. Apache vs. proprietary).
Domain-2.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you export models to run on different infrastructure?
  • Are models in standard formats (ONNX, TensorFlow SavedModel)?
  • Can you switch inference providers without retraining?
  • Do you have vendor lock-in for model deployment?
Domain-2.6-recommendation:
What is Model Portability?

Model Portability ensures models can be deployed across different infrastructure providers, edge devices, or on-premises systems without retraining or vendor-specific modifications.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate use of standard model formats (ONNX, TensorFlow SavedModel) that enable cross-platform deployment. Test model portability by deploying to at least two different infrastructure platforms.

Technical Recommendations

Convert models to ONNX format for maximum portability. Use containerization (Docker/Podman) to package models with their dependencies, enabling consistent deployment across environments.
Domain-2.6-redhat-description: Enterprise Kubernetes platform enabling portable deployment of AI models across on-premises, cloud, and edge environments with consistent tooling and APIs, eliminating vendor lock-in.
Domain-2.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you audit the algorithms and decision logic in your models?
  • Do you document model training processes and hyperparameters?
  • Can regulators inspect your model behavior and fairness?
  • Do you have processes to detect algorithmic bias?
Domain-2.7-recommendation:
What is Algorithmic Transparency?

Algorithmic Transparency provides visibility into how AI models operate, enabling regulatory audits, fairness verification, and accountability for automated decisions.

Executive Recommendations

Establish Algorithmic Transparency Standards documenting model design, training procedures, bias mitigation strategies, and fairness metrics. Prepare for regulatory audits required by EU AI Act and similar frameworks.

Technical Recommendations

Maintain comprehensive model documentation including training data characteristics, preprocessing steps, feature engineering, and fairness testing results. Implement bias detection and mitigation throughout the model lifecycle.
Domain-2.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have a formal AI model governance policy?
  • Who approves models for production deployment?
  • How do you handle model retirement and decommissioning?
  • Do you have a Model Risk Management framework?
Domain-2.8-recommendation:
What is Model Governance?

Model Governance establishes policies, procedures, and oversight for the entire AI model lifecycle from development through retirement, ensuring models are developed responsibly, deployed safely, and monitored continuously.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a Model Governance Committee with cross-functional representation (legal, compliance, data science, business) to approve high-risk model deployments. Implement Model Risk Management (MRM) framework aligned with industry standards.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy model governance platforms that enforce approval workflows, track model lifecycle stages, and maintain audit trails. Implement automated model monitoring to detect drift, performance degradation, or fairness issues.

Domain-3.overview:
AI Infrastructure Sovereignty ensures your organization has independent control over the compute, storage, and networking resources required for AI/ML workloads.
  • Sovereign Compute: Independent GPU/accelerator resources for training and inference.
  • Infrastructure Control: Ownership of AI infrastructure deployment and configuration.
  • Resource Independence: Ability to scale AI workloads without vendor constraints.
  • Multi-Cloud Flexibility: Freedom to deploy AI across infrastructure providers.
Domain-3.title: AI Infrastructure Sovereignty
Domain-3.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Where are your GPU/TPU resources located (cloud, on-prem, hybrid)?
  • Do you have guaranteed access to compute for critical AI workloads?
  • Can you scale GPU resources without vendor approval?
  • What happens if your cloud GPU provider has shortages?
Domain-3.1-recommendation:
What is Sovereign GPU Access?

Sovereign GPU & Accelerator Resources ensures your organization has reliable, independent access to the computational power required for AI training and inference without dependence on scarce cloud resources or vendor allocation policies.

Executive Recommendations

Develop a hybrid GPU strategy combining on-premises GPU infrastructure for critical workloads with cloud resources for burst capacity. Negotiate reserved GPU capacity agreements with cloud providers to ensure availability.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy on-premises GPU clusters for sensitive or regulated AI workloads. Use Kubernetes-based orchestration to enable portability of GPU workloads across on-prem and cloud environments.
Domain-3.1-redhat-description: Enterprise Kubernetes platform with GPU operator support, enabling consistent orchestration of GPU workloads across on-premises, cloud, and edge infrastructure for maximum sovereignty and flexibility.
Domain-3.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are AI training environments isolated from production systems?
  • Can you prevent data leakage between training and other workloads?
  • Do you use dedicated infrastructure for sensitive model training?
  • How do you isolate multi-tenant AI workloads?
Domain-3.2-recommendation:
What is Training Environment Isolation?

AI Training Environment Isolation ensures AI/ML training workloads are segmented from production systems and other tenants, preventing data leakage, resource contention, and cross-contamination of sensitive workloads.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate dedicated training infrastructure for high-risk or regulated AI use cases. Implement network segmentation between training, development, and production AI environments.

Technical Recommendations

Use Kubernetes namespaces, network policies, and resource quotas to isolate training workloads. Implement pod security policies to prevent privilege escalation and container escape in multi-tenant training clusters.
Domain-3.2-redhat-description: Provides enterprise-grade multi-tenancy with namespace isolation, network segmentation, and security policies to safely isolate AI training workloads while maintaining operational efficiency.
Domain-3.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Where are trained models and artifacts stored?
  • Do you control the model registry or use vendor-managed services?
  • Can you export all models from your registry?
  • How do you prevent unauthorized model downloads?
Domain-3.3-recommendation:
What is Model Registry Control?

Model Registry Control ensures trained models, artifacts, and metadata are stored in sovereign-controlled repositories, enabling version control, access governance, and independent model lifecycle management.

Executive Recommendations

Deploy self-hosted model registries rather than relying on vendor-managed services. Implement access controls and audit logging for all model downloads and deployments.

Technical Recommendations

Use open-source model registry solutions (MLflow, DVC) deployed on sovereign infrastructure. Implement RBAC to control who can register, download, or deploy models. Enable versioning and immutability for production models.
Domain-3.3-redhat-description: Can serve as a sovereign model artifact registry, storing ML models as container images or OCI artifacts with role-based access control, versioning, and geo-replication capabilities.
Domain-3.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you run distributed training across multiple nodes/GPUs?
  • Do you control the orchestration of distributed training jobs?
  • Can you scale training workloads horizontally?
  • What frameworks do you use for distributed training?
Domain-3.4-recommendation:
What is Distributed Training Orchestration?

Distributed Training Orchestration provides the ability to coordinate multi-node, multi-GPU training jobs across infrastructure, enabling faster model training while maintaining control over resource allocation and job scheduling.

Executive Recommendations

Invest in distributed training capabilities to reduce dependency on large cloud GPU instances. Use Kubernetes-based orchestration for portability across infrastructure providers.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy distributed training frameworks (Horovod, PyTorch DDP, DeepSpeed) on Kubernetes using operators. Implement gang scheduling to ensure all training pods start simultaneously for optimal performance.
Domain-3.4-redhat-description: Provides distributed training capabilities with support for popular frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow) and gang scheduling, enabling efficient multi-node GPU training on sovereign infrastructure.
Domain-3.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • How do you prioritize and schedule AI/ML workloads?
  • Can you guarantee GPU resources for critical training jobs?
  • Do you have fair-share scheduling for multiple teams?
  • How do you handle GPU resource contention?
Domain-3.5-recommendation:
What is AI Workload Scheduling?

AI Workload Scheduling ensures fair, efficient allocation of expensive GPU and accelerator resources across teams, projects, and workloads while meeting SLAs for critical AI applications.

Executive Recommendations

Implement multi-tenant scheduling policies with resource quotas per team/project. Establish SLAs for production inference workloads and implement priority-based scheduling.

Technical Recommendations

Use advanced Kubernetes schedulers (e.g., Volcano, Kueue) that understand GPU requirements and can implement fair-share scheduling. Deploy resource quotas and limit ranges to prevent resource monopolization.
Domain-3.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Where do you run model inference (on-prem, cloud, edge)?
  • Can you switch inference providers without code changes?
  • Do you have vendor lock-in for model serving?
  • Can you run inference offline or disconnected from cloud?
Domain-3.6-recommendation:
What is Inference Infrastructure Independence?

Inference Infrastructure Independence ensures models can be deployed and served across any infrastructure (cloud, on-prem, edge) without vendor-specific dependencies, enabling optimal placement based on latency, cost, and sovereignty requirements.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate use of standard inference serving frameworks (TorchServe, TensorFlow Serving, KServe) rather than proprietary vendor solutions. Test inference portability by deploying to multiple environments.

Technical Recommendations

Containerize inference services with all dependencies to enable consistent deployment across environments. Use inference frameworks that support multiple model formats and can run on CPUs or GPUs depending on performance requirements.
Domain-3.6-redhat-description: Self-hosted inference server enabling sovereign deployment of AI models on-premises or in controlled cloud environments with support for multiple model formats and optimized performance.
Domain-3.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you deploy AI models to edge devices independently?
  • Do you have control over edge AI infrastructure?
  • Can you update edge models without cloud connectivity?
  • How do you manage model distribution to edge locations?
Domain-3.7-recommendation:
What is Edge AI Deployment?

Edge AI Deployment enables running AI inference at edge locations (factories, retail stores, vehicles) for low latency, data sovereignty, and operation during network disconnection.

Executive Recommendations

Develop edge AI strategy for use cases requiring low latency or data residency at edge locations. Invest in edge infrastructure management platforms for consistent deployment and updates.

Technical Recommendations

Use lightweight Kubernetes distributions (MicroShift, K3s) for edge AI deployments. Implement model optimization techniques (quantization, pruning) to reduce model size for edge deployment. Deploy GitOps workflows for automated model updates to edge locations.
Domain-3.7-redhat-description: Lightweight platform for deploying and managing AI workloads at the edge with support for disconnected operations, automated updates, and consistent management across distributed edge locations.
Domain-3.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you monitor and optimize GPU utilization?
  • Can you identify idle or underutilized AI resources?
  • Do you have cost allocation for AI workloads by team/project?
  • Can you predict AI infrastructure costs for budgeting?
Domain-3.8-recommendation:
What is AI Infrastructure Cost Optimization?

AI Infrastructure Cost Optimization ensures efficient use of expensive GPU and accelerator resources through monitoring, rightsizing, and cost allocation, preventing wasteful spending on idle infrastructure.

Executive Recommendations

Implement FinOps practices for AI with chargeback or showback models to attribute costs to teams and projects. Establish GPU utilization KPIs and regularly review for optimization opportunities.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy GPU monitoring tools to track utilization, memory usage, and idle time. Implement auto-scaling for inference workloads and job preemption for low-priority training jobs. Use spot instances or interruptible workloads where appropriate to reduce costs.

Domain-4.overview:
AI Supply Chain Sovereignty addresses the security, transparency, and control of the AI software supply chain, from model provenance to dependency management.
  • Model Provenance: Verifiable origins and authenticity of AI models and components.
  • Dependency Security: Control over third-party libraries and frameworks used in AI systems.
  • Supply Chain Risk: Protection against compromised models, poisoned datasets, and malicious dependencies.
  • Transparency: Visibility into the complete AI supply chain from data to deployed model.
Domain-4.title: AI Supply Chain Sovereignty
Domain-4.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you verify the origin and authenticity of models you deploy?
  • Do you use cryptographic signatures for model artifacts?
  • Can you trace models back to their training source?
  • How do you prevent deployment of tampered or poisoned models?
Domain-4.1-recommendation:
What is Model Provenance Verification?

Model Provenance & Authenticity Verification ensures you can cryptographically verify that AI models are from trusted sources, haven't been tampered with, and can be traced back to their training lineage.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate model signing and verification for all production model deployments. Reject unsigned models or models from untrusted sources. Implement a trusted model registry with provenance tracking.

Technical Recommendations

Use cryptographic signing (GPG, Sigstore) for all model artifacts. Implement Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for models including training data hash, code commit, and dependencies. Verify signatures before model deployment.
Domain-4.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you use pre-trained models from public repositories (Hugging Face, etc.)?
  • How do you assess security risks of third-party models?
  • Do you scan models for backdoors or malicious behavior?
  • What vetting process exists for external model sources?
Domain-4.2-recommendation:
What is Third-Party Model Risk Assessment?

Third-Party Model Risk Assessment evaluates security, licensing, and operational risks of using pre-trained models from external sources like Hugging Face, GitHub, or vendor model hubs.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a Model Approval Process requiring security review before adopting third-party models. Maintain a whitelist of approved model sources and versions.

Technical Recommendations

Scan third-party models for known vulnerabilities, backdoors, or anomalous behavior. Use model analysis tools to inspect model weights for unusual patterns. Mirror approved models to internal repositories rather than pulling directly from external sources at deployment time.
Domain-4.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you track all Python/R packages used in AI projects?
  • Can you identify vulnerable dependencies in ML pipelines?
  • Do you pin dependency versions for reproducibility?
  • How do you handle transitive dependencies in AI workloads?
Domain-4.3-recommendation:
What is AI Dependency Management?

AI Dependency Management tracks and secures all third-party libraries, frameworks, and packages used in AI/ML development and deployment, preventing supply chain attacks through compromised dependencies.

Executive Recommendations

Implement Software Composition Analysis (SCA) for all AI projects, scanning for known vulnerabilities in Python packages, ML frameworks, and dependencies. Mandate dependency pinning for production deployments.

Technical Recommendations

Use dependency management tools (pip-tools, Poetry, conda) to create reproducible environments with version locking. Scan dependencies with tools like Safety, pip-audit, or Snyk. Maintain private package mirrors for critical dependencies.
Domain-4.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you verify integrity of training datasets before use?
  • Can you detect if training data has been poisoned or modified?
  • How do you secure data ingestion pipelines?
  • Do you use checksums or hashing for dataset verification?
Domain-4.4-recommendation:
What is Training Data Supply Chain Security?

Training Data Supply Chain Security ensures the integrity and authenticity of datasets used for model training, protecting against data poisoning attacks where malicious actors inject corrupted data to compromise model behavior.

Executive Recommendations

Implement dataset integrity verification using cryptographic hashing. Establish secure data ingestion processes with access controls and audit logging. Require approval for new data sources entering training pipelines.

Technical Recommendations

Generate and verify SHA-256 hashes for all training datasets. Implement data validation pipelines that check for statistical anomalies, outliers, or distribution shifts that may indicate poisoning. Store immutable copies of approved training datasets.
Domain-4.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you scan container images used for AI workloads?
  • Can you detect vulnerabilities in base images (CUDA, PyTorch, etc.)?
  • Do you have policies blocking deployment of vulnerable images?
  • How often do you rebuild images to patch vulnerabilities?
Domain-4.5-recommendation:
What is Model & Container Image Scanning?

Model & Container Image Scanning identifies security vulnerabilities in the container images used to package and deploy AI models, ensuring the entire runtime environment is free from known exploits.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate automated image scanning in the CI/CD pipeline with policies blocking deployment of critical vulnerabilities. Establish SLAs for patching vulnerabilities in AI container images.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate container image scanning tools (Clair, Trivy, Anchore) into model deployment pipelines. Use minimal base images to reduce attack surface. Implement automated image rebuilds when vulnerabilities are discovered in base layers.
Domain-4.5-redhat-description: Includes built-in security scanning with Clair integration, automatically detecting vulnerabilities in container images used for AI model deployment and providing compliance reporting.
Domain-4.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you generate SBOMs for AI models and applications?
  • Can you list all components in a deployed AI system?
  • How do you track when vulnerable components are deployed?
  • Can you respond quickly to zero-day vulnerabilities in AI dependencies?
Domain-4.6-recommendation:
What is AI Software Bill of Materials?

AI Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) provides a comprehensive inventory of all components, libraries, models, and dependencies in an AI system, enabling rapid response to security vulnerabilities and supply chain incidents.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate SBOM generation for all AI applications using standard formats (SPDX, CycloneDX). Maintain a centralized SBOM repository for vulnerability tracking and compliance reporting.

Technical Recommendations

Use SBOM generation tools (syft, trivy) to automatically create SBOMs during build processes. Include model metadata, Python packages, system libraries, and base container images. Integrate SBOM data with vulnerability databases for continuous monitoring.
Domain-4.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you attest that models were built using approved processes?
  • Do you use SLSA framework or similar supply chain standards?
  • Can you prove models weren't tampered with during deployment?
  • How do you demonstrate supply chain compliance to auditors?
Domain-4.7-recommendation:
What is Supply Chain Attestation?

Supply Chain Attestation provides cryptographic proof that AI models and applications were built, tested, and deployed using approved processes, meeting compliance requirements like SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts).

Executive Recommendations

Adopt SLSA framework or similar supply chain security standards for AI systems. Implement build attestation to prove models come from trusted build environments. Prepare for regulatory requirements around AI supply chain transparency.

Technical Recommendations

Use Sigstore or similar tools to generate signed attestations for build provenance. Implement policy engines (OPA, Kyverno) that verify attestations before allowing model deployment. Store attestations alongside models in the registry.
Domain-4.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you monitor for new vulnerabilities in deployed AI components?
  • Can you identify when vendor models are compromised?
  • How quickly can you respond to supply chain security incidents?
  • Do you have rollback procedures for compromised models?
Domain-4.8-recommendation:
What is Continuous Supply Chain Monitoring?

Continuous Supply Chain Monitoring tracks deployed AI systems for emerging vulnerabilities, compromised dependencies, and supply chain incidents, enabling rapid detection and response to security threats.

Executive Recommendations

Establish 24/7 supply chain monitoring with automated alerting for critical vulnerabilities in deployed AI systems. Define incident response procedures for supply chain compromises including rollback and patching workflows.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate vulnerability databases (CVE, OSV) with your model registry and deployment systems. Implement automated scanning of deployed systems to detect outdated or vulnerable components. Use runtime monitoring to detect anomalous behavior that may indicate compromised models.

Domain-5.overview:
AI Governance & Compliance ensures your organization has policies, oversight, and controls to manage AI systems responsibly and meet regulatory requirements.
  • Policy Framework: Formal AI governance policies and standards.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Adherence to AI regulations (EU AI Act, etc.).
  • Ethics & Fairness: Responsible AI practices and bias mitigation.
  • Accountability: Clear ownership and oversight of AI systems.
Domain-5.title: AI Governance & Compliance
Domain-5.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have a formal AI governance policy?
  • Who is responsible for AI governance in your organization?
  • Are AI policies aligned with broader IT governance?
  • How do you communicate AI policies to teams?
Domain-5.1-recommendation:
What is AI Governance Policy?

AI Governance Policy Framework establishes the foundational policies, standards, and procedures that govern how AI systems are developed, deployed, and operated across the organization.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a Chief AI Officer or AI Governance Committee with authority to set AI policies and standards. Document AI governance framework covering development standards, risk management, and accountability.

Technical Recommendations

Create technical standards for AI development including model documentation requirements, testing standards, and deployment approval processes. Integrate AI governance into existing IT governance and risk management frameworks.
Domain-5.2: Regulatory Compliance Tracking (EU AI Act, etc.)
Domain-5.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Which AI regulations apply to your organization (EU AI Act, GDPR, etc.)?
  • Do you classify AI systems by risk level as required by regulations?
  • Can you demonstrate compliance with AI transparency requirements?
  • How do you stay updated on evolving AI regulations?
Domain-5.2-recommendation:
What is AI Regulatory Compliance?

AI Regulatory Compliance ensures your AI systems meet emerging legal requirements like the EU AI Act, which classifies AI systems by risk and imposes transparency, accountability, and safety requirements.

Executive Recommendations

Conduct AI system inventory and risk classification according to applicable regulations. Assign legal counsel to monitor AI regulatory developments. Prepare for increased documentation and transparency requirements.

Technical Recommendations

Implement AI system registry tracking risk classification, intended use, and compliance status. Develop compliance checklists for high-risk AI systems covering data governance, model documentation, and human oversight requirements.
Domain-5.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have documented AI ethics principles?
  • How do you ensure AI systems are fair and unbiased?
  • Do you have processes to identify harmful AI use cases?
  • Who reviews AI systems for ethical concerns?
Domain-5.3-recommendation:
What is AI Ethics Framework?

AI Ethics & Responsible AI Principles establish the moral and ethical guidelines for AI development and deployment, ensuring AI systems are fair, transparent, and beneficial while avoiding harm.

Executive Recommendations

Adopt Responsible AI Principles (e.g., fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy) aligned with frameworks like IEEE, OECD, or internal values. Establish an ethics review process for high-risk AI use cases.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate fairness metrics and bias testing into the model development lifecycle. Use AI ethics checklists during model design and deployment reviews. Provide responsible AI training for data science and engineering teams.
Domain-5.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you test AI models for bias before deployment?
  • What fairness metrics do you measure (demographic parity, equal opportunity)?
  • Can you detect bias in training data?
  • How do you mitigate identified biases?
Domain-5.4-recommendation:
What is Bias Detection & Fairness Testing?

Bias Detection & Fairness Testing systematically evaluates AI models for discriminatory behavior across protected attributes (race, gender, age, etc.), ensuring equitable treatment and compliance with anti-discrimination laws.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate fairness testing for all AI systems making decisions about people (hiring, lending, healthcare, etc.). Establish acceptable fairness thresholds and require mitigation before production deployment.

Technical Recommendations

Use fairness testing frameworks (AI Fairness 360, Fairlearn, What-If Tool) to measure disparate impact across demographic groups. Implement bias mitigation techniques (reweighting, adversarial debiasing, etc.). Document fairness test results for audit purposes.
Domain-5.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you conduct risk assessments for AI systems?
  • How do you classify AI systems by risk level?
  • What controls exist for high-risk AI applications?
  • Do you have AI incident response procedures?
Domain-5.5-recommendation:
What is AI Risk Management?

AI Risk Management identifies, assesses, and mitigates risks associated with AI systems including model failures, security vulnerabilities, ethical concerns, and operational impacts.

Executive Recommendations

Adopt AI Risk Management Framework (e.g., NIST AI RMF) to systematically assess and manage AI risks. Require formal risk assessments for high-risk AI systems before deployment. Establish AI incident response procedures.

Technical Recommendations

Develop risk assessment templates covering model performance risks, security risks, bias risks, and operational risks. Implement tiered controls based on risk classification (low/medium/high risk systems). Conduct regular risk reviews of deployed AI systems.
Domain-5.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Who approves models for production deployment?
  • Do you have formal approval workflows for AI changes?
  • How do you manage model updates and versioning?
  • Can you rollback models if issues arise?
Domain-5.6-recommendation:
What is Model Approval & Change Management?

Model Approval & Change Management establishes formal processes for reviewing, approving, and tracking changes to AI models throughout their lifecycle, ensuring governance and accountability.

Executive Recommendations

Implement model approval workflows requiring sign-off from stakeholders (data science, legal, compliance, business) before production deployment. Define change management procedures for model updates.

Technical Recommendations

Use workflow automation tools to enforce approval gates in model deployment pipelines. Implement blue-green or canary deployment strategies for model updates. Maintain rollback procedures and ensure previous model versions remain available.
Domain-5.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you maintain comprehensive audit logs for AI systems?
  • Can you demonstrate decision-making history for models?
  • Are model development processes documented?
  • Can you produce documentation for regulatory audits?
Domain-5.7-recommendation:
What is AI Audit Trail?

AI Audit Trail & Documentation maintains comprehensive records of AI system development, deployment, and operation, enabling regulatory compliance, incident investigation, and continuous improvement.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate comprehensive documentation for all production AI systems including model cards, datasheets, development history, and deployment records. Prepare for regulatory audits requiring proof of responsible AI practices.

Technical Recommendations

Implement MLOps platforms with built-in audit logging. Generate model cards documenting intended use, training data, performance metrics, and limitations. Maintain immutable audit logs of all model training, deployment, and inference activities.
Domain-5.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • How do you evaluate AI vendors for compliance and governance?
  • Do you have vendor risk assessment processes for AI services?
  • Can you audit third-party AI systems you depend on?
  • What contractual protections exist for AI vendor relationships?
Domain-5.8-recommendation:
What is Third-Party AI Vendor Governance?

Third-Party AI Vendor Governance ensures external AI service providers meet your organization's governance, security, and compliance requirements, preventing risk transfer through vendor relationships.

Executive Recommendations

Develop AI vendor assessment framework covering data governance, model transparency, security, and compliance. Require contractual clauses addressing liability, audit rights, and data ownership for AI services.

Technical Recommendations

Conduct technical due diligence on AI vendors including security assessments, model transparency reviews, and compliance verification. Implement vendor risk scoring and regular re-assessment. Maintain vendor registry with governance status.

Domain-6.overview:
AI Operations Sovereignty ensures your organization can independently operate, monitor, and maintain AI systems in production without external dependencies.
  • Operational Independence: Ability to run AI systems without vendor operational support.
  • Monitoring & Observability: Complete visibility into AI system performance and behavior.
  • Incident Response: Independent capability to diagnose and resolve AI incidents.
  • Performance Management: Control over AI system optimization and scaling.
Domain-6.title: AI Operations Sovereignty
Domain-6.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you monitor AI model accuracy and performance in production?
  • Can you detect when model performance degrades?
  • Do you track model drift (data drift, concept drift)?
  • What alerts exist for model performance issues?
Domain-6.1-recommendation:
What is AI Model Performance Monitoring?

AI Model Performance Monitoring tracks model accuracy, precision, recall, and other metrics in production to detect degradation, drift, or unexpected behavior that may require retraining or intervention.

Executive Recommendations

Establish model performance SLAs and implement continuous monitoring to ensure models maintain acceptable accuracy levels. Define thresholds for automated alerting when performance degrades.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy model monitoring solutions that track prediction accuracy, confidence scores, and business metrics. Implement automated drift detection for input data and model predictions. Use A/B testing to validate model improvements before full deployment.
Domain-6.1-redhat-description: Provides integrated model monitoring capabilities with drift detection, performance metrics tracking, and alerting to ensure AI models maintain quality in production.
Domain-6.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have centralized logging for AI inference requests?
  • Can you trace individual predictions through the system?
  • Do you monitor latency and throughput of AI services?
  • Can you correlate AI logs with application logs?
Domain-6.2-recommendation:
What is AI System Observability?

AI System Observability provides comprehensive logging, metrics, and tracing for AI services, enabling troubleshooting, performance optimization, and compliance auditing.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate comprehensive logging for all AI inference requests including inputs, outputs, latency, and model versions. Implement log retention policies that balance compliance needs with storage costs.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy centralized logging (ELK, Loki) and distributed tracing (Jaeger, Tempo) for AI services. Implement structured logging with correlation IDs for request tracing. Monitor infrastructure metrics (GPU utilization, memory, network) alongside application metrics.
Domain-6.2-redhat-description: Provides comprehensive logging, metrics, and distributed tracing capabilities with sovereign data storage, enabling complete observability of AI workloads without external dependencies.
Domain-6.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can your team troubleshoot AI issues without vendor support?
  • Do you have runbooks for common AI operational issues?
  • Can you access model internals for debugging?
  • What happens if vendor support is unavailable?
Domain-6.3-recommendation:
What is Independent AI Troubleshooting?

Independent Troubleshooting & Support ensures your operations team can diagnose and resolve AI system issues without reliance on external vendor support, maintaining operational continuity.

Executive Recommendations

Invest in AI operations training for internal teams covering model debugging, performance tuning, and incident response. Develop runbooks for common AI operational scenarios.

Technical Recommendations

Use open-source AI frameworks where source code is available for deep debugging. Maintain detailed documentation of AI system architecture, dependencies, and troubleshooting procedures. Build internal expertise through training and knowledge sharing.
Domain-6.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have incident response procedures for AI failures?
  • Can you quickly rollback problematic model deployments?
  • How do you handle AI-related security incidents?
  • What is your RTO/RPO for AI systems?
Domain-6.4-recommendation:
What is AI Incident Response?

AI Incident Response & Recovery establishes procedures for detecting, responding to, and recovering from AI system failures, security incidents, or performance degradation.

Executive Recommendations

Develop AI-specific incident response playbooks covering model failures, data quality issues, bias incidents, and security breaches. Define RTO/RPO targets for critical AI services.

Technical Recommendations

Implement automated circuit breakers that fail gracefully when AI models malfunction. Maintain fallback mechanisms (rule-based systems, previous model versions). Conduct incident response drills for AI-specific scenarios.
Domain-6.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you retrain models independently without vendor assistance?
  • How often do you retrain production models?
  • Do you have automated retraining pipelines?
  • Can you perform emergency model updates if needed?
Domain-6.5-recommendation:
What is Model Retraining Operations?

Model Retraining & Update Operations ensures you can independently refresh models with new data, fix performance issues, or adapt to changing conditions without external dependencies.

Executive Recommendations

Establish model refresh schedules based on drift detection and business requirements. Invest in automated retraining pipelines that can be triggered on-demand for urgent updates.

Technical Recommendations

Build automated retraining pipelines with data validation, training execution, model evaluation, and deployment stages. Implement canary deployments to test retrained models before full rollout. Document retraining procedures and requirements.
Domain-6.5-redhat-description: Provides automated MLOps pipelines for model retraining with integrated scheduling, data validation, and deployment workflows, enabling independent model lifecycle management.
Domain-6.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you optimize model latency and throughput independently?
  • Do you use model optimization techniques (quantization, pruning)?
  • Can you tune inference performance without vendor tools?
  • How do you balance accuracy vs. performance?
Domain-6.6-recommendation:
What is AI Performance Optimization?

AI Performance Optimization Capabilities enable independent tuning of model inference speed, resource utilization, and cost efficiency while maintaining acceptable accuracy levels.

Executive Recommendations

Establish performance SLAs for AI services (latency, throughput) and invest in optimization capabilities to meet targets without vendor reliance. Balance performance with model accuracy based on business requirements.

Technical Recommendations

Implement model optimization techniques including quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation, and hardware-specific optimizations. Use profiling tools to identify inference bottlenecks. Test optimizations thoroughly to ensure accuracy is maintained.
Domain-6.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have DR plans specific to AI systems?
  • Can you recover AI services to alternate infrastructure?
  • Are model artifacts backed up and recoverable?
  • How do you test AI disaster recovery procedures?
Domain-6.7-recommendation:
What is AI Disaster Recovery?

AI Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity ensures AI systems can be restored in alternate locations or infrastructure in the event of catastrophic failures, maintaining business operations.

Executive Recommendations

Include AI systems in enterprise DR planning with specific RTO/RPO targets. Test DR procedures regularly including failover to backup infrastructure and model artifact restoration.

Technical Recommendations

Implement geo-redundant storage for model artifacts and training data. Document dependencies and deployment procedures to enable recovery on alternate infrastructure. Maintain DR runbooks specific to AI system recovery.
Domain-6.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you track and optimize AI operational costs independently?
  • Do you have visibility into inference costs per request?
  • Can you identify cost optimization opportunities?
  • How do you forecast AI operational expenses?
Domain-6.8-recommendation:
What is Operational AI Cost Management?

Operational AI Cost Management provides visibility and control over ongoing AI infrastructure and service costs, enabling optimization without vendor lock-in or dependency on proprietary cost management tools.

Executive Recommendations

Implement AI cost tracking and attribution to understand spending by model, team, or business unit. Establish cost optimization KPIs and regularly review for efficiency opportunities.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy cost monitoring tools that track AI infrastructure usage (compute, storage, network). Implement cost allocation tags for AI workloads. Use autoscaling and spot instances where appropriate to reduce costs. Monitor cost-per-inference metrics.

Domain-7.overview:
AI Innovation Sovereignty ensures your organization can independently innovate, experiment, and advance AI capabilities without restrictions from vendors or external dependencies.
  • Innovation Freedom: Ability to experiment with new AI techniques and approaches.
  • Research & Development: Independent AI R&D capabilities.
  • Competitive Advantage: Proprietary AI innovations that differentiate your organization.
  • Talent & Skills: Internal AI expertise and knowledge development.
Domain-7.title: AI Innovation Sovereignty
Domain-7.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have dedicated AI R&D teams and resources?
  • Can you experiment with new AI techniques independently?
  • Do you contribute to AI research or rely solely on vendors?
  • What percentage of AI capability comes from internal development?
Domain-7.1-recommendation:
What is Internal AI R&D?

Internal AI Research & Development establishes organizational capability to explore, experiment with, and develop novel AI techniques, reducing dependence on vendor innovation roadmaps.

Executive Recommendations

Allocate budget for AI R&D initiatives separate from production AI operations. Create dedicated time for data scientists to experiment with new techniques and contribute to open-source AI projects.

Technical Recommendations

Provide AI R&D teams with sandbox environments, access to research papers, and compute resources for experimentation. Encourage participation in AI conferences and research communities. Establish processes to transition successful experiments to production.
Domain-7.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have platforms for rapid AI experimentation?
  • Can data scientists access compute resources on-demand?
  • Do you use MLOps tools for experiment tracking?
  • How quickly can you test new AI ideas?
Domain-7.2-recommendation:
What is AI Experimentation Platform?

AI Experimentation Platform & Tools provide self-service infrastructure and tooling enabling data scientists to rapidly test hypotheses, iterate on models, and validate new AI approaches.

Executive Recommendations

Deploy self-service AI development platforms that reduce time-to-experiment from weeks to hours. Remove barriers to innovation by providing easy access to compute, data, and collaboration tools.

Technical Recommendations

Implement JupyterHub or similar platforms for interactive development. Provide experiment tracking tools (MLflow, Weights & Biases) for managing trials. Enable on-demand GPU access with autoscaling to support experimentation bursts.
Domain-7.2-redhat-description: Provides self-service AI development environment with Jupyter notebooks, experiment tracking, and on-demand compute resources, accelerating innovation cycles and enabling data scientists to iterate rapidly.
Domain-7.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you contribute to open-source AI projects?
  • Can your team participate in AI research communities?
  • Do you use and customize open-source AI frameworks?
  • What is your strategy for open-source AI engagement?
Domain-7.3-recommendation:
What is Open Source AI Participation?

Open Source AI Contribution & Participation enables your organization to influence AI technology direction, access cutting-edge innovations, and avoid vendor lock-in through active engagement with open-source communities.

Executive Recommendations

Develop open-source AI strategy outlining which projects to support, contribution policies, and IP management. Allow employees to contribute to open-source projects during work time where aligned with business interests.

Technical Recommendations

Standardize on open-source AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) rather than proprietary alternatives. Encourage data scientists to participate in open-source communities. Contribute improvements and bug fixes back to projects you depend on.
Domain-7.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you build custom AI models from scratch?
  • Do you rely primarily on pre-trained vendor models?
  • What percentage of models are custom-developed vs. vendor-provided?
  • Can you fine-tune models for your specific use cases?
Domain-7.4-recommendation:
What is Custom AI Model Development?

Custom AI Model Development Capabilities enable building proprietary models tailored to unique business requirements, providing competitive advantage beyond what off-the-shelf vendor models can deliver.

Executive Recommendations

Invest in AI engineering talent capable of custom model development. Identify use cases where custom models provide competitive differentiation worth the investment vs. using pre-trained models.

Technical Recommendations

Build expertise in model architecture design, training optimization, and hyperparameter tuning. Use transfer learning and fine-tuning to adapt foundation models to specific domains. Maintain libraries of reusable model components and training utilities.
Domain-7.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you have programs to develop internal AI expertise?
  • Can you retain top AI talent against vendor competition?
  • Do you provide ongoing AI training and upskilling?
  • What is your AI talent acquisition and retention strategy?
Domain-7.5-recommendation:
What is AI Talent Development?

AI Talent Development & Retention builds internal AI expertise through training, career development, and knowledge sharing, reducing dependence on external consultants and vendor professional services.

Executive Recommendations

Establish AI career paths with clear progression from junior to senior roles. Provide ongoing training in emerging AI techniques. Create AI centers of excellence to share knowledge across the organization.

Technical Recommendations

Implement AI training programs for existing staff to upskill into AI roles. Provide access to online courses, conferences, and certifications. Create internal knowledge sharing through brown bags, code reviews, and documentation.
Domain-7.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you own proprietary AI algorithms or techniques?
  • Have you filed patents for AI innovations?
  • Do you have trade secrets in your AI systems?
  • How do you protect AI intellectual property?
Domain-7.6-recommendation:
What is Proprietary AI IP?

Proprietary AI Intellectual Property represents unique AI innovations, algorithms, or techniques that provide competitive advantage and are protected through patents, trade secrets, or other IP mechanisms.

Executive Recommendations

Develop AI IP strategy identifying which innovations to patent, which to keep as trade secrets, and which to contribute to open source. Review AI projects for patentable innovations.

Technical Recommendations

Document novel AI techniques and algorithms developed internally. Implement access controls and confidentiality measures to protect proprietary AI IP. Use invention disclosure processes to identify patentable AI innovations.
Domain-7.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you partner with universities for AI research?
  • Can you access cutting-edge AI research?
  • Do you participate in industry AI consortia?
  • How do you stay ahead of AI technology trends?
Domain-7.7-recommendation:
What is AI Academic & Industry Partnerships?

AI Academic & Industry Partnerships provide access to cutting-edge research, emerging techniques, and collaborative innovation opportunities beyond internal capabilities.

Executive Recommendations

Establish strategic partnerships with leading AI research institutions and industry consortia. Sponsor AI research projects aligned with business priorities. Recruit PhD interns to bring fresh perspectives.

Technical Recommendations

Collaborate with universities on joint research projects. Participate in industry working groups developing AI standards and best practices. Sponsor conference workshops or challenges to engage with research community.
Domain-7.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Does your culture encourage AI experimentation and risk-taking?
  • How do you handle AI project failures and learning?
  • Do you have innovation time or hackathons for AI?
  • How do you measure and reward AI innovation?
Domain-7.8-recommendation:
What is AI Innovation Culture?

AI Innovation Culture & Practices establish organizational norms, processes, and incentives that encourage creative experimentation, calculated risk-taking, and continuous learning in AI development.

Executive Recommendations

Foster innovation-friendly culture that accepts failure as part of the learning process. Sponsor AI hackathons and innovation challenges. Recognize and reward successful AI innovations with tangible incentives.

Technical Recommendations

Implement '20% time' or innovation days for AI experimentation. Create safe-to-fail environments where teams can test bold ideas. Share learnings from both successes and failures. Celebrate innovation attempts, not just outcomes.
